title: Return Merchandise Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: Set the return merchandise inspection scope, test readiness and requirement-level evidence, contain deficiencies, authorize status, and preserve qualified closeout.
description: An original, fillable return merchandise inspection checklist form for controlling returned product, return authorization, and disposition unit through inspection checklist identity, observations, evidence, decision, exceptions, escalation, completion, handoff, and final verification without replacing applicable requirements or professional review.
use_case: Use when a returns authorization coordinator or qualified inspector must evaluate returned product, return authorization, and disposition unit against the return authorization, original sale, product identity, and return policy and provide a traceable basis for release, restriction, hold, correction, or rejection.

sections.title: Return Merchandise inspection checklist identity and routing
sections.guidance: Anchor the record to the exact work, parties, locations, and source references.

fields.label: Return authorization and original order number
SKU, serial, lot, package, or return-label ID

blocks.label: Responsible parties and route points

fields.label: Customer, store, field location, or return carrier
Returns dock, quarantine area, repair, restock, or supplier route

blocks.guidance: Preserve linkage to the return authorization, original sale, product identity, and return policy.

sections.title: Return Merchandise inspection scope, criteria, and readiness
sections.guidance: Define the exact population and review basis so inspection conclusions remain bounded.

fields.label: Returned Product, Return Authorization, And Disposition Unit
Return Authorization, Original Sale, Product Identity, And Return Policy

blocks.label: Return Merchandise readiness verification
items: Return authorization, original transaction, customer, and item are matched
Permitted quantity, return reason, return window, and routing are explicit
Serial, lot, warranty, ownership, and recall status can be verified
Required accessories, packaging, manuals, keys, or components are identified
Data-bearing, hazardous, contaminated, food, and temperature-sensitive items are routed
Carrier label, pickup method, and receiving destination are correct
Refund, replacement, repair, restock, supplier return, and disposal authority are separated
Fraud, privacy, safety, and unresolved-condition escalation is assigned
blocks.guidance: A failed readiness item must be resolved, excluded with rationale, or carried into the exception section.

sections.title: Return Merchandise requirement-level inspection results
sections.guidance: Record actual observations against explicit criteria and identify the evidence for each result.

blocks.label: Return Merchandise detailed inspection points
items: Return authorization and original order identify the received item
SKU, model, serial, lot, and quantity match the approved return scope
Product and package condition are photographed before handling changes
Accessories, manuals, cables, keys, parts, or bundled items are reconciled
Tamper, use, installation, contamination, or modification evidence is recorded
Recall, warranty, ownership, and data-bearing status are checked
Hazardous, leaking, sharp, swollen, contaminated, or unsafe item is isolated
Temperature-sensitive item remains held pending disposition when control is uncertain
Restock, repair, supplier return, credit, or disposal criteria are not assumed
Unresolved identity, condition, safety, or policy issue is routed to qualified review
blocks.guidance: Checkboxes indicate that the point was examined; the result table carries findings and evidence.

sections.title: Return Merchandise measurements and evidence package
sections.guidance: Preserve readings, instruments, identity, and evidence needed to reproduce the inspection decision.

blocks.label: Measurement, count, or verification log
blocks.guidance: Use the method applicable to Authorized, received, accepted, and disposition quantity and Product, packaging, accessory, seal, and use condition.

blocks.label: Available inspection evidence
items: Return authorization and original transaction
Carrier tracking and return-label identity
Arrival and unopened-package photographs
Serial, lot, model, and ownership verification
Accessory and component reconciliation
Inspection and functional-test reference
Customer communication and promised remedy
Approved disposition, credit, repair, or supplier route

blocks.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

fields.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

sections.title: Return Merchandise exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, affected scope, immediate control, owner, deadline, and escalation reconstructable.

blocks.label: Return Merchandise exception indicators
items: No valid return authorization or item outside approved scope
SKU, serial, lot, ownership, or original transaction cannot be matched
Received quantity or accessories differ from the return request
Undisclosed use, damage, contamination, modification, or missing parts
Hazardous, leaking, swollen, sharp, or otherwise unsafe condition
Data-bearing device lacks approved privacy handling
Temperature control or product integrity cannot be established
Warranty, recall, return-window, or policy status is disputed
Customer remedy and physical disposition conflict
Duplicate credit, replacement, or return record is suspected
blocks.guidance: Select every observed condition; do not use a generic exception mark when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Return Merchandise inspection status and release decision
sections.guidance: Do not turn a checklist score into release when a critical exception or evidence gap remains.

fields.label: Returns, Quality, Or Finance Supervisor review

sections.title: Return Merchandise inspection checklist closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: Use this return merchandise inspection checklist with the applicable customer commitment, carrier terms, site policy, and retention requirements. Do not infer acceptance or release from a signature alone; unresolved identity, count, condition, custody, or proof issues require an owner, escalation, and documented disposition.

blocks.label: Prepared, reviewed, and accepted

fields.label: Reviewed by returns, quality, or finance supervisor

blocks.guidance: A signature records accountability for the stated decision; it does not cure missing evidence or override a stop condition.
